messages:
alex (support): FYI ticket from ZenFleet - their dedicated pool `zenfleet-prod` hit a large TPS spike ~2026-03-16T20:14Z. Customers saw 429s with 'admission_rejected' and generation latency > 5s. They report burst credits at 0 in the console and autoscaling didn't appear to add replicas.
zenfleet_ops (quoted customer): "We had a campaign send about 3x normal traffic for ~90s. SDK calls started failing at 20:14:12, error: 429 AdmissionControl: tokens-per-second exceeded. Console shows \"burst credits: 0 / regen_rate 10/s\" and requests queued then dropped. Can you restore service for the campaign?"
alex (support): Paste of the customer error snippet: ```ERROR 2026-03-16T20:14:13Z request_id=ab12ad admission_rejected reason=burst_credits_exhausted tokens_requested=1500```
mike (sre): Looking at the cluster: `zenfleet-prod` has reserved capacity 4x A100s, min_replicas=2; HPA didn't scale because GPU util stayed ~40% (requests are short but bursty). Admission controller uses token-bucket sized by tps_headroom and burst_credits. If credits hit 0 it will reject.
jordan (infra): Confirming: autoscaler didn't kick because pod CPU/GPU metrics didn't breach thresholds; we rely on request rate-based scaling in the serving runtime but that's tuned to steady-state throughput to avoid flapping. Short 90s spike can exhaust credits before scaling acts.
tanya (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation options: 1) top-up burst credits for zenfleet-prod (temp) 2) lower admission threshold (allow slightly higher p99 latency) 3) enable fallback to hosted-compat model variant in region while dedicated regains headroom. Recommend 1+3 immediate.
alex (support): Customer asked for immediate fix. I can grant temporary credits but need approval from infra on how to do it safely. Any script?
mike (sre): Use ops-bot runbook: `ops-bot grant-burst --pool zenfleet-prod --amount 20000 --ttl 30m` (this increments the token bucket). Will also add a short-lived admission-policy override: `admission.override(zenfleet-prod, allow_extra_headroom=1.2, ttl=30m)`. ops-bot?
ops-bot: Runbook executed: grant-burst succeeded (granted 20000 tokens, expires 30m). Admission override applied (ttl 30m). Audit id: RB-20260316-447.
jordan (infra): I've also patched a short-lived scaling hint: increased request-rate sensitivity so the serving runtime can spawn 1 extra replica faster for the next 10m. This is safe - will roll back after 10m.
zenfleet_ops (quoted customer): "Thanks — we see errors dropping and throughput returning to normal. Can you explain why this happened and what prevents it in future?"
tanya (eng-runtime): Root cause notes: burst saw many concurrent high-token requests (longer contexts + streaming) from a single tenant. Token-bucket regeneration is tuned for usual traffic; autoscaling reacts to sustained GPU pressure not 30-90s microbursts. Also, a noisy neighbor (another tenant) had a long KV-cache-heavy request that transiently increased memory pressure and slowed response times, which increased token hold-time and accelerated credit burn.
mike (sre): Immediate follow-ups: 1) Post-mortem to capture traffic pattern, exact token math, and why request-rate-based scaling didn't trigger quick enough. 2) Add an emergency pre-warm policy for customers with predictable campaigns (allow pre-allocating short burst credits). 3) Evaluate lowering the HPA scale-in cooldown / add a burst-mode HPA trigger based on request concurrency.
jordan (infra): Action items assigned: - jordan: export full serving logs + admission metrics for 20:00-20:30 (in ticket) - tanya: simulate same burst in staging to repro (include token sizes and streaming keepalive) - mike: draft temporary customer playbook for granting credits + risk checklist.
alex (support): I'll reply to customer with timeline and ops-bot audit id. Also offering guidance: pre-warm / schedule campaigns, or request dedicated burst plan.
tanya (eng-runtime): Long-term engineering proposals: - add a short-timescale rate-based scaler in runtime (sub-minute) - make burst credit regen dynamic by observed token hold-time - implement per-customer soft-fallback to hosted variant with preserved auth & keys when dedicated pool is saturated.
mike (sre): Ticket updated #ZEN-4981. Planning post-mortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT with eng-runtime + infra + support.
alex (support): Customer updated: "All good now — thanks for quick help. We'll coordinate future campaigns." :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Reminder: RB-20260316-447 will expire in 25m. Please confirm if you want to extend.
jordan (infra): I'll leave it to eng-runtime to decide extension after repro.
(timeline/meta) alex (support): first report 1891122334, mitigation applied 1891122380, last observed error 1891122440.
